name: TX-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbency advantage with no polling to suggest a race
Markets price Ellzey at ~95% to win
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Ellzey's incumbency, and a roughly 100-to-1 fundraising edge leave Minton with no visible path, and prediction markets agree at about 95% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings showing any competitive signal, this sits at the Safe R threshold.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Minton within single digits, or major outside spending entering the district, would warrant moving this toward Likely R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Ellzey seeks a third full term in a North Texas district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $4.7 million and holding $2.5 million on hand, while Democrat Danny Minton has raised about $44,000. No public polls or expert ratings target the race, and prediction markets give Ellzey roughly a 95 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the partisan lean, incumbency, and the money gap all favor the Republican, with only a modest offset from the national environment. The forecast expects Ellzey to win by roughly fifteen points, consistent with both the district's lean and the absence of any evidence of a competitive race.
